title: Wasserstein HMM Explainable Regime-Aware Portfolio Allocation on SPY/TLT/GLD
description: Implement an explainable regime-aware portfolio construction framework using a Wasserstein Hidden Markov Model (Wasserstein HMM) on the SPY/TLT/GLD 3-asset universe. The Wasserstein HMM combines rolling Gaussian HMM inference with predictive model-order selection and template-based identity tracking using the 2-Wasserstein distance between Gaussian components. This allows the number of regimes to adapt dynamically while preserving stable economic interpretation (regimes don't randomly swap labels). Regime probabilities are then embedded into a transaction-cost-aware mean-variance optimization framework. Key innovation over H383 (plain HMM+RL): (1) Wasserstein distance for regime identity tracking prevents the label-switching problem that makes plain HMM regimes uninterpretable across time; (2) dynamic model-order selection vs fixed 3-state assumption; (3) explicit transaction cost penalty in the optimization layer reduces unnecessary rebalancing. Universe: SPY/TLT/GLD/BIL (add BIL as 4th safe-haven asset). Data: daily 2004-2026. IS: 2004-2017, OOS: 2018-2026. Gate: OOS Sharpe > 1.532 (H311 EW-4+VIX<20 best multi-asset baseline) AND MaxDD < -10%. Implementation: Python, hmmlearn, scipy (Wasserstein distance via scipy.stats.wasserstein_distance or POT library), cvxpy for optimization. CAVEAT: use filtered (not smoothed) regime probabilities to avoid look-ahead bias per Regime Detection Design Note.
rationale: Boukardagha (2026) arXiv:2603.04441 reports Sharpe 2.18 vs 1.59 equal-weight on a diversified daily cross-asset universe, with MaxDD of -5.43% vs -14.62% for SPY buy-and-hold. The model dynamically reduced equity exposure during the early 2025 'Liberation Day' selloff, validating real-world regime detection. The Wasserstein identity tracking directly addresses the key weakness in H251 (plain HMM predicted low-vol 100% of OOS months — regime labels collapsed). This is a clean, interpretable extension of our confirmed H311 multi-asset framework. Transaction-cost-aware optimization layer also addresses H273's leveraged ETF concern by penalizing excess turnover. Columbia University, March 2026.
